Applicant-Prem Sagar Alias Sonu Singh, who is a named as well as charge sheeted accused and facing trial before Court below, has approached this Court by means of present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.. with the following prayer:-
"It is therefore, most respectfully that this Hon'ble court may graciously be pleased to quash the entire further proceedings in Criminal Case No. 149 of 2020 (State Vs.
Premsagar @ Sonu Singh) arising out of charge sheet and order of cognizance dated 17.03.2020 passed by Special Judge POCSO Act, Court No.1, Kushinagar in the offence registered in Case Crime No. 306 of 2019 under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and POCSO Act, at Police Station- Ramkola, District-Kushinagar, pending before Special Judge POCSO Act, Court No.1, Kushinagar.

8. Learned counsel for applicant submit that though applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused and facing trial before Court below, however in view of the peculiar facts and circumstance of the case as have now emerged on record, the criminal prosecution of applicant cannot be sustained any further.
As such, the present application is liable to be allowed and impugned proceedings pending against applicant before Court below are, therefore, liable to be quashed by this Court.

2 9.

sentences.text: In furtherance of above submission urged by the learned counsel for applicant it is pointed out that during pendency of aforementioned criminal case, the parties amicably settled their dispute outside the Court.
On the basis of settlement so arrived at between the parties, a compromise was entered into.

Subsequently, the terms of the compromise were reduced in writing by way of a compromise deed dated 27.04.2024, copy of which has been brought on record and appended as annexure-6 to the affidavit filed in support of this application.

10. It is then contended by the learned counsel for applicant that upto this stage, two prosecution witnesses of fact i.e. PW-1 Junab Ali (Father of the prosecutrix) and PW-2 prosecutrix have deposed before Court below who have not supported the FIR.

On the strength of above, the learned counsel for applicant submits that since dispute between the parties is a purely private dispute and not a crime against state/society, therefore, the impugned proceedings can be terminated in view of the compromise entered into by the parties.
In view of the compromise entered into by the parties, the chances of conviction of accused-applicant is not only remote but also bleak.
As such, no useful purpose shall now be served in prolonging the criminal prosecution of applicant.
On the above premise, it is thus urged by the learned counsel for applicant that present applicantion is liable to be allowed by this Court.

11. At this juncture, the Court raised a pointed query as to whether the said compromise entered into by the parties, copy of which has been brought on record and appended as annexure-6 to the affidavit filed in support of this application has been filed before Court below or not.
12. Learned counsel for applicant fairly submits that said compromise deed has not yet been filed before Court below.
13. On the above premise, the learned A.G.A. thus submits that there is no such material on record on the basis of which it can be conclusively concluded that parties have entered into a compromise.

Learned A.G.A. has then referred to the judgment of Supreme Court in State of Kerala VS. Hafsal Rahman N.R., Special Leave Petition (Criminal) Diary Nos. 24362 of 2021, wherein it has been observed that there can be no compromise in matters under the POCSO Act.

entities.text: State of Kerala VS. Hafsal Rahman N.R., Special Leave Petition (Criminal) Diary Nos. 24362 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is then submitted by the learned A.G.A. that once the trial of the applicant has commenced before court below and two prosecution of witnesses of fact i.e. PW-1 and PW-2 have deposed before Court below then applicant can either be acquitted of the charges alleged against him or he can be convicted on account of the charges having been proved against him.

Simply on an angular version of the crime in question as per the statements of PW-1 and PW-2, this Court in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. cannot quash the proceedings of trial pending against applicant accused before Court below.

It is thus urged by the learned A.G.A. that present application is wholly misconceived and therefore,
liable to be dismissed.
14. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

15. Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State-opposite party-1 and upon perusal of record, this Court finds that the objection raised by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to this application are not only borne out from the record but furthermore the same could not be Prem Sagar Alias Sonu Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151183344/
3 dislodged by the learned counsel for applicant with reference to the record.

entities.text: Prem Sagar Alias Sonu Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of above, no good ground exists to entertain the present application.
16. As a result, the present application fails and is liable to be dismissed.
17. It is, accordingly, dismissed.
